input.question: Which person or organization did Ben F. Spencer work for?

documents.text: As Dr. Sophia Patel poured over the dusty archives in the basement of Edinburgh Napier University's Sighthill campus, she stumbled upon a forgotten folder with a faded label: "Spencer, B.F. - Research Collaborations (2005-2008)". The name sparked a faint memory, and Sophia's curiosity was piqued. She delicately opened the folder, releasing a whisper of aged paper and forgotten dreams. Inside, she found a collection of yellowed documents, meeting minutes, and scribbled notes. The handwriting was messy, but the ideas were revolutionary. Sophia's eyes widened as she read about Ben F. Spencer's groundbreaking research on sustainable energy harvesting. The concepts were ahead of their time, and Sophia couldn't help but wonder why they had been shelved. As she delved deeper into the folder, Sophia discovered a series of emails between Ben and his colleagues, discussing the potential applications of his research. The tone was enthusiastic, with a hint of frustration. It seemed that Ben's innovative ideas had been met with skepticism by the university administration. Sophia's brow furrowed as she read about the bureaucratic red tape that had slowed Ben's progress. Suddenly, a faint noise echoed from the corner of the archive room. Sophia looked up to see a bespectacled archivist, Mrs. MacTavish, peering over the rim of her reading glasses. "Ah, you've found the Spencer files," she said, her voice laced with a hint of nostalgia. "Ben was a brilliant mind, but a bit of a rebel. He didn't suffer fools gladly." Sophia's eyes locked onto Mrs. MacTavish. "Did you know him?" she asked, her voice barely above a whisper. Mrs. MacTavish nodded, her eyes clouding over. "Aye, I did. Ben was a researcher here at Edinburgh Napier University. He was part of our team, working on a project to develop sustainable energy solutions for rural communities. He was passionate, driven... and a bit of a thorn in the side of our administrators." As Sophia listened, Mrs. MacTavish's words painted a vivid picture of Ben F. Spencer - a maverick researcher who had pushed the boundaries of innovation, even if it meant ruffling a few feathers. The forgotten folder, once a relic of a bygone era, now held a new significance.
